fault: The your keyboard does not power on: no backlight and no response when plugged in.
diagnosis: A keyboard that is completely dead is usually a cable, port or mode problem, not a bad switch. I will have you unplug it, check the cable and USB-C port, check the mode switch, then plug it back in and test.
safety_notes: Unplug the keyboard before cleaning the USB-C port.
Touch grounded metal before handling the board to avoid static damage.
Never push anything metal into the USB-C port.

steps.title: Unplug the keyboard
steps.instruction: Pull the USB-C cable out of the back of the keyboard. Touch grounded metal first.
steps.expected_visual_state: No cable is in the USB-C port and the backlight is off.
common_mistakes: Leaving the cable plugged in while checking the board.
Reaching for the board without grounding yourself first.

steps.title: Inspect the USB-C port
steps.instruction: Look into the USB-C port on the keyboard. Blow out any dust or lint with compressed air.
steps.expected_visual_state: The USB-C port is visible and clear of dust, with the metal tongue inside intact.
common_mistakes: Poking the port with a metal object.
Missing lint packed deep in the port that stops the plug seating.

steps.title: Check the mode switch
steps.instruction: Slide the mode switch on the back edge to the wired USB position. Make sure it is not in the off position.
steps.expected_visual_state: The mode switch sits fully in the wired position, not between positions and not off.
common_mistakes: Leaving the switch in the off or Bluetooth position.
Stopping the slider halfway between two positions.

steps.title: Swap in a different cable
steps.instruction: Take a spare USB-C data cable and plug the keyboard end in firmly. Plug the other end straight into the computer, not a hub.
steps.expected_visual_state: A different USB-C cable is fully seated in the keyboard port and connected to the computer.
common_mistakes: Using a charge-only cable that carries no data.
Not pushing the plug fully into the port.

steps.title: Plug in and test
steps.instruction: Check that the backlight comes on. Press a few keys and see them type on the screen.
steps.expected_visual_state: The cable is plugged in, the backlight is lit, and pressed keys type on screen.
common_mistakes: Not testing more than one key.
Expecting backlight when it is turned down to off with the brightness keys.
